This is a desirable outcome, as it indicates that the model is able to learn and generalize from the ground truth, and is not relying too heavily on its own internal state. A larger ratio implies that the model is able to effectively use the ground truth to inform its generation, and is therefore more efficient and effective in minimizing repetition.

On the other hand, a smaller ratio would indicate that the model is generating the same output with more repetitions when given its own prefix, compared to when it is given a ground truth prefix. This would be a less desirable outcome, as it suggests that the model is not learning and generalizing from the ground truth, and is instead relying too heavily on its own internal state.

Therefore, in the context of minimizing repetition, a larger ratio is indeed better.
